notes: SHIP v1.14.419 - P1 OF PHASE-ENGINE: THE EVENT LOG, FOLDED IN WITHOUT BREAKING THE CHAIN. No UI surface. THE FOLD. The governing spec describes an append-only Event Log with no edits and no deletes, where corrections are new entries referencing the old id. That log already existed as phantom_deploy_audit_v1, and it already had the harder half: hash chaining via prevHash and a self-hash, tamper evidence through deploy_verifyAuditChain, and a chainReset marker so FIFO eviction is visible rather than silent. Owner ruled FOLD rather than build a second store - a parallel Event Log would be the duplicate state this programme exists to delete, and it would arrive without the chain. THE TRAP THIS SHIP EXISTS TO AVOID, FOUND BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN. The hash is taken over a FIXED FIELD LIST, and deploy_verifyAuditChain RE-HASHES each STORED entry with that list before comparing it to the digest the entry was written with. Simply appending the five spec fields to that list would have re-hashed every pre-existing entry under a wider canonical form, produced a different digest for all of them, and made the chain report TAMPERING across the operator entire history - on a device where nothing was wrong. A tamper-evident log that cries wolf is worse than not having one: it destroys the single signal it exists to give. THE FIX IS A VERSIONED CANONICAL FORM. Each entry records the version it was hashed under and is verified under THAT version. v1 entries have no hashV and keep verifying exactly as they always did; v2 entries carry hashV 2 and are hashed over the wider set. Neither generation is ever hashed under the other schema. It is self-protecting: flipping hashV on a v2 entry to make it verify as v1 changes the field set, so the digest fails either way. The truncation fields (chainReset, truncatedCount, truncatedAt, truncatedLastHash) remain deliberately OUTSIDE the hashed set, because the FIFO path mutates an entry after its hash was taken - the wider v2 set does not sweep them in. AUTOMATIC PROVENANCE, OPTIONAL DETAIL. siteProfileId and masterId are NOT passed by callers - they are stamped here, from the profile and the live Master, at write time. That is what makes spec section 4.3 work: events survive a Master swap carrying the truth-context that produced them, without twenty-five call sites having to remember to attach it. rack, stepId and evidence come from an OPTIONAL sixth meta argument; all twenty-five existing five-argument callers are untouched and keep working. TESTS: new spec 11-event-log.spec.js, six tests, all green. The one that matters is the first: an entry written under v1 still verifies after P1 exists. Also pinned: a new entry is v2 and carries the section 6.3 fields with provenance stamped automatically; the old five-argument call still chains; a MIXED v1-then-v2 chain verifies end to end and links correctly; editing masterId after the fact BREAKS the chain, which proves the new fields are genuinely covered rather than decorative; and annotating an entry with truncation metadata does not read as tampering. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the commit hook. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: no visible surface. Confirm v1.14.419, then open the audit log and confirm your history is intact and reports no tampering. In the console, deploy_verifyAuditChain() must return ok true with brokenAt null.
